summary: Both majors are genuinely closed and I measured rather than accepted them. MAJOR 1: in my own tree the round-3 mutant -- `if (chainEpoch >= 1) { crossFromCheckpoint(hops, chainEpoch, limit); }` in the neverOpened branch, folding the checkpoint and then adding the full Hop anyway -- now FAILS aRunOfBURNEDEpochsStillStopsAtTheCheckpointBehindThem on the count at 55 requests against the bound of 15, and deleting the probe outright fails at 52. The staged tree measures 11, and 11 is the same number the 4-delta fixture produced, so the assertion is flat in the ancestor's chain length rather than merely small. The fixture is sound: K is the 4th CheckpointWriter argument and is injected at 1, so epoch 1's newest checkpoint covers all forty deltas; epoch 2 is genuinely burned, so the walk reaches the arithmetic branch, which is the only thing that reaches this probe; the offsets assertion (40) still kills a cross that stops the walk without folding. `<= 15` is meaningful at 40 deltas -- an unbounded walk is 52-55 -- though it carries 4 requests of slack, which is the second minor. MAJOR 2: 29/46/80/148/284 matches the series I measured myself in round 3, and matches ADR-0035, the class javadoc and the backlog row at every site; `git grep -E '17/26|32/43|62/77|122/145|242/281|26/43/77/145/281|3/4/6/10/18'` finds only retractions plus the open-spec row in backlog-notes.md, which stays verbatim by the convention every other done row follows. The attribution at ChainReplay.java:161 is NOT accurate, and that is minor 1: `which M4.6e measured growing 29/46/80/148/284 ... -- measured HERE, on this harness, not carried from a row` asserts two contradictory authors in one sentence, and M4.6e is still the wrong one. The MINOR is fixed correctly -- the K IS INJECTED AT 1 paragraph is back on `takeoverCost`, which is the declaration it documents. Removing the fifteen dead imports broke nothing: `./gradlew test` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL across every module in my tree. No request-rate finding in this delta: it adds no store call, and the walk's cost scales with epochs walked and stops at the first checkpoint, so it scales with failovers, not with records, streams or indices.

findings.title: The ChainReplay comment still says M4.6e measured the series, in the same sentence that says it was measured here -- the attribution half of M4.9-R3-2 is unclosed, not fixed
findings.rule: non-negotiable 4 (never claim a number was measured without having measured it)
findings.failure_scenario: Line 158-162 now reads `a takeover costs O(all commit-log entries ever written), which M4.6e measured growing 29/46/80/148/284 requests at 1/2/4/8/16 prior terms -- measured HERE, on this harness, not carried from a row.` The grammatical subject of `measured` is still M4.6e, and the trailing clause asserts the opposite about the same numbers. M4.9-R3-2 named both halves: the retracted series AND `the attribution is wrong too -- M4.6e's own backlog-done row does not carry that table, so `M4.6e measured` names a measurement M4.6e never made`. The numbers half was fixed at every site; the attribution half was left standing and a contradicting clause bolted onto it. Failure scenario: a session chasing the provenance of the before-series -- which is what the whole round-3 finding was about -- reads `M4.6e measured`, greps M4.6e's row and `git log M4.6e` for the table, finds nothing, and either re-measures or concludes the comment is stale in some unknown way. ADR-0035 records the truth (`re-measured on 15da3fb`, which is M4.8c, the commit immediately before this one), so the canonical record is right and only this comment is wrong -- which is why it is minor rather than major: the load-bearing part, the numbers a future session would transcribe, is correct and consistent everywhere. The remedy is deleting two words: `which this commit measured growing 29/46/80/148/284 requests ... on this harness (ADR-0035)`. Not fixing it is permitted under minors-land; if it is left, the honest form is to say so in the commit body rather than leave the sentence self-contradicting.

findings.title: The new burned-epoch bound is an inequality with 4 requests of measured slack, fifty lines below a comment in the same file declaring `this is the only absolute number on the bounded path` and that `an inequality leaves room a regression can live in`
findings.rule: cost.md R9 (count requests through the decorator); review.md failure-scenario
findings.mutation: Add one request per chain probed -- e.g. a second stat, or a get, issued once per iteration of replayAncestry's while loop.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED: the staged tree issues 11 requests through CountingBinStore in this test (I replaced the assertion with isEqualTo(0L) and read the failure), against the asserted bound of 15. This walk crosses three chains (3 -> 2 -> 1), so a regression costing one extra request per chain probed lands at 14 and passes -- exactly the room the sibling assertion's own comment at line 250-259 refuses to leave, twenty-five lines above: `EXACT, like the failover test's counts and for the same reason: an inequality leaves room a regression can live in`. That comment now also carries two claims this change made false in the same file: `Every other cost assertion in this file compares two MEASUREMENTS` and `this is the only absolute number on the bounded path`. There is now a second absolute number on the bounded path, fifty lines below, and it is not exact. This is the shape the task's own row records twice -- a javadoc contradicted by a change twenty lines away, and an `.as()` label claiming coverage that does not exist. The bound does its job against both mutants I measured (55 and 52 against 15), so this does not block; the fix is isEqualTo(11L) plus a one-line correction to the sibling comment, and per minors-land it is as defensible to record it in the commit body. Deliberately NOT filed: the doubled paragraph at lines 250-259 (`AN ABSOLUTE COUNT` and `EXACT, like the failover test's` say the same thing twice) and the triple blank line at line 100 predate this round.
